newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts buoyant, Bulgaria rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts buoyant, Bulgaria rebounds.

text.p: In a market flush with liquidty, most emerging market debt prices rose smartly on Wednesday.

Attention focused on Mexico, but the nation's early repayment of the emergency loan to the U.S. Treasury and the International Monetary Fund failed to give its Bradies a significant boost, traders said.
At 1615 EST, Mexico PARs were down 1/8 at 74 flat, and Mexico 2008s were 1/8 higher at 99-5/8.

Earlier, Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Mexico would immediately repay the outstanding $3.5 billion of an emergency loan from the U.S. Treasury and would also repay early $1.5 billion owed to the International Monetary Fund.
"Generally, the news in the market is very positive with Mexico's announcement that it is repaying $5 billion early," said Joyce Chang, emerging markets debt stategist for Merrill Lynch & Co.
Argentina Bradies, in contrast, enjoyed a strong rally.
"There has been some solid buying from all sectors of the world," said a trader at a U.S. investment house.
He said Argentina was the flavor of the day inspired by expected demand for the upcoming $2.0 billion global issue.
Agrentina FRBs gained 3/4 to 89-1/4 bid, while Argentina discounts surged 1-1/4 to 80-3/8 bid.
Bulgaria Bradies that appeared "exceptionally cheap" have rallied, Chang said.
Fresh signs of early election agreements between Bulgarian's ruling Socialists and opposition may have alleviated some investors' jitters over the country's political pains, another trader said.
Bulgarian IABs were up 1-1/4 at 51-1/2 bid and Bulgarian DISCs were 1-1/8 higher at 56-7/8 bid.
Panama Bradies climbed amid speculation that the sovereign credit would get rated in the near term with a possible BB or BB-plus rating, said Merrill Lynch's Chang.
Panama IRBs advanced 1-1/8 to bid at 71-1/2 by late afternoon Wednesday, and Panama PDIs were up 1-1/4 at 81-1/8 bid.
